issues.description: Packetization buffers any bytes payload, not just audio frames, corrupting non-audio binary messages.
issues.detail: _write_frame slices every bytes payload into fixed_audio_packet_size chunks whenever the param is set. A serializer emitting a non-audio bytes payload (control messages, headers) gets chopped into PCM-sized chunks. Gate on AudioRawFrame type rather than `isinstance(payload, bytes)` before treating bytes as PCM.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has no invariant tying it to sample width/channels, silently corrupting audio on misconfiguration.
issues.detail: The param is an untyped int with no precondition that it be a multiple of (bytes_per_sample * channels). A value like 641 on 16-bit mono PCM produces half-sample tearing at every packet boundary and noise on the receiver. State the invariant and enforce it (assert or raise on StartFrame/setup).

issues.description: Trailing audio in send buffer and resampler tail are never flushed on shutdown/EOS.
issues.detail: On disconnect, StopFrame, or end-of-stream, the residual _audio_send_buffer (0 to packet_bytes-1 bytes) is discarded, and the streaming resampler's internal tail is also dropped because serialize/deserialize bail when len == 0. The 'all serialized audio reaches the wire' postcondition is silently weakened. Either flush (pad with silence) or document the lossy contract.

issues.description: Real-time pacing claim is unsupported: send loop has no clock gate and may bypass _next_send_time bookkeeping.
issues.detail: The changelog promises 'real-time pacing,' but _write_frame drains the buffer in a tight `while` loop with immediate awaits and no wall-clock invariant binding emissions to _next_send_time. The early return after the loop also skips the pacing/bookkeeping the normal path performs. Either the existing pacing handles this and the comment misleads, or this path breaks it.

issues.description: DTMF deserialization accepts two undocumented digit shapes with no spec reference.
issues.detail: deserialize tries message.get('digit') then message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit'). Two accepted shapes with no citation pins the contract to observation rather than the Vonage spec. Pick the documented shape and reject or shim the other with a TODO; otherwise protocol drift hides here forever.

issues.description: PCM16 format is asserted in comments but never enforced; non-PCM16 input is resampled as garbage.
issues.detail: Comments in serialize/deserialize claim 16-bit linear PCM, but no check on frame.format or sample width exists. Upstream code handing 8-bit or float audio results in garbage being resampled and shipped. A one-line assert or precondition check beats a comment and would catch misconfiguration loudly.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The Vonage serializer itself is a reasonable ADT, but the FastAPI packetization path is too eager: it treats any bytes payload as PCM, lacks an alignment invariant on fixed_audio_packet_size, drops trailing audio at shutdown, and does not actually implement the wall-clock pacing the changelog promises. Secondary issues are an under-specified DTMF digit shape and unenforced PCM16 assumptions in serializer comments. Fix the frame-type gating, state and enforce the packet-size invariant, wire flush-on-EOS, and pin the DTMF schema before merge.
